I don’t think this should be a partisan issue. I also don’t think it’s a black-and-white issue.

From his private journal entries, it appears Fauci considered the possibility of a lab-related origin while continuing to lean toward a natural origin based on the evidence available at the time. The entries reflect uncertainty and ongoing evaluation rather than certainty in either direction. 

The funding trail itself is relatively clear. NIH, through NIAID, awarded a grant to EcoHealth Alliance, which then subcontracted about $600,000 over several years to the Wuhan Institute of Virology. That funding supported coronavirus research. The fact that U.S. government money reached the Wuhan lab isn’t really disputed.

Where the disagreement begins is how to interpret that funding. Some argue the experiments amounted to gain-of-function research under the government’s own definitions, while others argue they did not under the rules in place at the time. That’s a genuine scientific and regulatory dispute, not simply a factual one.

My view is that there are valid questions about oversight, transparency, and whether the public was given a complete picture early on. Those questions deserve serious scrutiny. At the same time, I don’t think the evidence publicly available today proves that Fauci intentionally funded the creation of COVID-19 or knowingly covered up its origin. It’s reasonable to criticize decisions and communication without jumping to conclusions that haven’t been established.
